newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude- North Asian buys light sweet cargoes.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude- North Asian buys light sweet cargoes.

text.p: Asian light crude prices strengthened on buying from China, South Korea and Thailand, traders said on Friday.
September cargoes of Griffin, Cossack and North West Shelf were confirmed done, but at cost and freight basis (c+f).
This led to mixed market opinions on where realistic levels should be on a free on board basis (fob), traders said.
A combi cargo of Griffin/North West Shelf was sold to a South Korean refiner at Tapis APPI +15 cents per barrel, and at Tapis APPI +$1.05 per barrel c+f respectively.
The seller reported the freight cost to be at 95 cents per barrel, which would netback to around Tapis APPI -80 fob for Griffin, and NWS APPI +10 fob for North west Shelf.
But some traders said freight should be closer to $1.05.
September Cossack was also sold by a producer to China at Tapis APPI +30 cents c+f.
Traders were also uncertain about Tapis price, as a shosha rumoured sold an August cargo to Thailand at APPI -20/40, a contrast to a September cargo sold by Malaysia at APPI +10/15.
Some traders said that September Tapis discounts have narrowed, in line with the stronger light crude market, but that buyers would be unwilling to pay a premium yet.
In Middle East crudes, Thailand bought one million barrels of September Oman, at MPM -2, but the price was unconfirmed.
A shosha also heard bought Oman at the same level, while two cargoes of Murban were heard sold to Japanese at ADNOPC +8.
